payoff: Design Spring Boot /live and /ready for slow startup, DB outage, recovery, and drain without creating restart loops.
learningOutcomes: definisikan /live dan /ready pada Spring Boot; simulasi DB down dan slow startup. Readiness menolak traffic saat unusable; liveness tidak membuat restart loop akibat kegagalan dependency sementara.
mentalModel: Process alive is not service ready: startup tolerates cold boot, liveness can trigger restart, readiness controls traffic, and graceful shutdown drains.
relationshipGraph: startupProbe -> process /live -> readiness(/ready: warmup + essential DB + drain) -> Service admission -> transfer business checks.

concepts.title: Liveness versus readiness
concepts.mechanism: Different Kubernetes probe failure reactions: restart versus traffic exclusion.

concepts.title: Spring Boot health groups
concepts.mechanism: Actuator health groups expose status and configurable additional server paths.

concepts.title: Slow startup protection
concepts.mechanism: Startup probes delay regular liveness/readiness until cold boot completes.

concepts.title: Shared DB readiness policy
concepts.mechanism: Use explicit bounded readiness checks for mandatory external dependencies, not liveness.

concepts.title: Graceful drain
concepts.mechanism: Shutdown drains in-flight requests while removing regular traffic endpoints.

segments.objective: Define /live and /ready as different Spring Boot health contracts.
segments.whyItMatters: An HTTP process may be healthy while a required ledger database cannot serve money movements.
segments.mentalModel: Liveness is process health and restart eligibility; readiness is traffic admission. Neither proves transaction safety.
segments.explanation: Spring Boot Actuator exposes /actuator/health/liveness and /actuator/health/readiness, and can add main-port aliases /live and /ready. Kubernetes uses liveness failure for restarts and readiness failure to remove normal Service traffic. The liveness group must not check external systems. Adding a DB indicator to readiness is an explicit critical-dependency decision; a shared DB outage may make all replicas unready.

steps.action: Keep the shared DB outside liveness.
steps.reason: Restarting replicas cannot repair the remote database.

steps.action: Make critical DB readiness explicit and bounded.
steps.reason: Unavailable instance should not receive normal transfer traffic.

segments.objective: Separate a startupProbe budget from readiness during warming.
segments.whyItMatters: A healthy process may take long to initialize before it can serve transfer operations.
segments.mentalModel: startupProbe defers regular liveness/readiness checks until it succeeds; readiness can still stay unready afterward.
segments.explanation: A startupProbe can protect slow cold boot. For example a 5-second period and failureThreshold of 24 give about 120 seconds of tolerated startup failures, not a precise timing guarantee. Once the HTTP listener is active, /live may return 200 while essential warmup continues and /ready returns 503. Probe settings must follow measured cold-start behavior, and the HTTP fixture does not implement actual kubelet scheduling.

segments.objective: Simulate DB outage and graceful shutdown without dependency-driven restart loops.
segments.whyItMatters: Shared DB failures and abrupt rollout termination can amplify incidents across replicas.
segments.mentalModel: A critical DB may affect readiness while a healthy process stays live. Draining stops new traffic while existing work completes within a bounded window.
segments.explanation: By default Spring Boot readiness does not include every external health indicator; operators must choose critical ones. When a required DB fails, readiness may report 503 and liveness should remain 200 if the process itself still progresses. DB recovery can restore readiness without restarting. On SIGTERM, graceful shutdown stops accepting new requests and gives in-flight requests a configured phase timeout; Kubernetes terminating endpoints are not eligible for regular Service traffic. An /live 200 is never permission to execute a financial operation.

workedExample.problem: Shared DB failures and abrupt rollout termination can amplify incidents across replicas.

steps.action: Simulate DB unavailable on a healthy process.
steps.reason: Availability of a shared dependency does not dictate local process death.
